data.why: The app bundles its own example datasets (fraud/AML synthetic, Curran 2021, Mondal 2025) loaded from app/data/, so no uploads are needed to run the main workflow; this one small unlabelled CSV (matching Curran 2021's 10 numeric predictor columns, with a missing value and an outlier) is provided so the Predict New Data tab can be exercised after fitting a model.

goals: Load a published binary astrophysical dataset (associated vs. intervening HI absorbers) and inspect class balance and feature distributions
Compare classifiers (XGBoost, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree) and class-imbalance strategies (none, class weighting, SMOTE, under-sampling) on a held-out stratified split
Evaluate precision, recall, F1, ROC/AUC and confusion matrices rather than relying on raw accuracy, especially for the rare-event fraud dataset
Tune the decision threshold away from the default 0.5 cutoff and examine the precision/recall/alert-rate trade-off
Inspect feature importance for the fitted model to see which spectral/behavioural parameters drive the classification
Apply the fitted model to fresh, unlabelled data and download the scored predictions

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose accurately: compare classifiers and imbalance methods, judge them by precision, recall, F1 and alert rate rather than accuracy, tune the threshold, and score new data. The 13 screens I opened back up every claim. To file it, the tasks need regrouping from the agent's tour into real stages, t9 needs to say it used seed 43, and three missing features need adding: the class-balance baseline, the plain-language summary, and the data loader.
